name: Two Pure Two-Unit Wings Force Three Independent Pairs
statement: Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$, and suppose both terminal wings have the pure $\eta=2$ two-apex form. Then three of their four terminal acquired direction pairs are pairwise disjoint.
proof: The two systems are internally disjoint and cannot repeat a pair across wings by shadow intersection. Without a matching of order three, their support graph is $C_4$, $P_5$, or $2P_3$. In the connected cases, the normal-form theorem produces an apex corner at passive distance two, contradicting passive radius-one shielding and cornerlessness. In the disconnected case, either a forced distance-one owner lies in $B$ or is forced into both disjoint exclusive sets, again impossible; or $B=P_9$ and both wings acquire the common collar pair $\{x_4,x_5\}$ although the tree $B$ shatters no pair, contradicting shadow intersection. Thus the matching must exist.
